sources.title: Batch 0062 frozen repository context for doubly-linked-list LRU
Independent doubly-linked LRU list-map differential validation
Batch 0062 doubly-linked LRU source-first isolated review

claims.text: The two preserved primary-source occurrences ask for a doubly-linked-list LRU implementation and do not prescribe Java, miss semantics, invalid capacity handling or concurrency behavior.

Under the declared positive-capacity single-threaded Java contract, the HashMap plus sentinel doubly-linked-list implementation matches an independent list-map LRU model on fixed boundaries and 45,000 random operations.

Independent validation covers miss behavior, read refresh, update refresh, capacity-one eviction and non-positive-capacity rejection while the answer keeps concurrency and richer cache policies outside the source contract.

boundary_tests.expected: both remain visible and map to the same canonical without pretending they are distinct question meanings
null according to explicit candidate contract
recently read key survives while older key is evicted
updated key refreshes to MRU and does not increase size
each distinct new key evicts the previous key
IllegalArgumentException according to explicit candidate contract
exact agreement with independent list-map LRU model

findings: Both frozen primary-source occurrences carry the same question asking specifically for a doubly-linked-list LRU implementation; the duplicate occurrence is preserved rather than collapsed, while the source does not prescribe language, API, miss value, invalid-capacity behavior or concurrency semantics.

The candidate directly addresses the requested data structure by pairing a HashMap index with a sentinel-based doubly linked list ordered MRU to LRU, instead of answering only with a generic cache abstraction.
The positive-capacity, single-threaded Java API and null-on-miss behavior are explicitly labeled as answer-level contract choices rather than source facts.
Read hits and updates both refresh recency, overflow removes tail.prev, and eviction removes the same key from the map, preserving the one-map-entry/one-list-node invariant.

The executable implementation is independently revalidated against a simple HashMap plus explicit recency-list oracle rather than the writer LinkedHashMap oracle, including capacity-one boundaries and 45,000 random operations.
Complexity wording correctly distinguishes strict O(1) pointer relinking from expected O(1) HashMap operations, avoiding an unsupported worst-case claim.
